VICI.thesis_one_line: Owns irreplaceable Las Vegas Strip and regional casino real estate on long, CPI-linked leases, priced far below what its steady growth and diversification deals justify.
kill_criteria: Combined Caesars + MGM share of total contractual rent stops declining and rises back above 75% for two consecutive quarters (from ~70% currently), signalling the diversification trend has reversed.
AFFO/share guidance is cut (any reduction to the low end of the then-current full-year range) at a subsequent release -- track record is currently four-for-four raises/holds.
Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 5.5x (from ~4.9x currently) without a stated deleveraging plan.
A monetary default, lease restructuring, or sub-investment-grade credit-rating downgrade (below B1/B+) at either Caesars or MGM.
Realized rent growth trails CPI by more than 100bps for two consecutive years, i.e. the escalator caps bind and erode real rental income (VICI's own disclosed risk).
key_adverse_facts: Caesars and MGM combined still supply ~70% of VICI's total contractual rent (Q2'26: Caesars 36%, MGM 34%; Q1'26: Caesars 37%, MGM 36%) -- an unusually concentrated two-tenant credit exposure for a REIT this size.

GAAP net income and EPS are highly volatile quarter to quarter (Q2'26 diluted EPS $0.48, down 39% YoY) on non-cash fair-value/credit-loss items in VICI's financing-receivable and preferred-equity book; the Q2'26 print was widely reported as an 'EPS miss' despite AFFO growing 7.8%.

Generic vendor free-cash-flow fields (Yahoo/d4) show only a ~1% FCF yield for VICI because REIT growth-capex ('PaymentsToAcquireRealEstate') is misclassified as a cash outflow against earnings -- AFFO, not FCF, is the correct metric, consistent with the program's known REIT-metric flaw already disclosed for HST/FRT.
Short interest rose ~22% between roughly year-start and end-April 2026 (to ~3.0% of float) -- still a low absolute level but a directionally more cautious positioning shift.
VICI.confidence_in_thesis: medium-high -- the value/income case is independently confirmed from primary filings and the guidance record is clean (4-for-4 raises), but tenant concentration is a real, unresolved structural risk that caps conviction below full weight [DV42 2026-10-08: scenario returns restated: bear -0.4% (was +4%), base +11.4%, bull +12.9% (was +18.5%); dividend is $0.45/qtr; AFFO/share growth 4.5-5.3% per quarter. Verdict unchanged.]

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for VICI (v1_valuation_table.csv has no VICI row; VICI appears only as a peer-comparison sample inside FRT's V1 detail JSON), so v1_verdict is null and no reconciliation is possible. This dossier's own reverse DCF (Gordon-growth on AFFO/share, price $23.51, AFFO guide $2.46/sh, required return 8.5-9.5%) implies perpetual AFFO/share growth of roughly -0.9% to -1.8% -- i.e. the market prices VICI as if AFFO per share will shrink forever -- versus an evidence-based base case of +3-4%/yr from CPI-linked escalators and demonstrated accretive acquisitions. Implied growth is clearly below base case: cheap, not merely fair.

APTV.thesis_one_line: Auto electrical/software supplier just cut its first post-spinoff full-year guidance; cheap and better-capitalized, but not yet proven stable.
kill_criteria: FY2026 guidance is cut again at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release (any further reduction to the low end of the current $12.6-12.8bn revenue / $5.60-5.80 adjusted-EPS range).
Non-automotive (software/AV/enterprise) segment revenue growth decelerates below 8% YoY for two consecutive quarters (from +12% in Q2'26).
Net debt/adjusted EBITDA rises above 3.0x (from ~2.0x post-spin) without a stated value-accretive reason.
Free cash flow for two consecutive quarters comes in below the low end of the then-current full-year FCF guidance range (currently $625-725M).
Top-5 customer concentration rises above 45% of net sales (from ~42%), or GM/Stellantis/Ford cuts North American production schedules by more than 5% for a full year.
key_adverse_facts: FY2026 guidance was cut on revenue, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS AND free cash flow simultaneously at the Q2'26 release (2026-08-04) -- just one quarter after 'New Aptiv' first issued post-spin guidance at Q1'26 -- for itemized reasons (China production-schedule changes ~$150m, delayed launches/ramps ~$100m, enterprise-software timing ~$50m). [DV04: the itemised $150m/$100m/$50m attribution is not in the Q2 8-K Ex-99.1 or 10-Q (unverified, likely from the call).]

Free cash flow was negative in Q1'26 and only $12m in Q2'26 (vs $219m a year earlier) even as adjusted EPS beat the prior-year figure; on a continuing-operations basis YTD FCF was -$196m vs +$264m (Q1'26 about -$208m; the -$362m quoted earlier is the consolidated figure including EDS) -- a real, current gap between adjusted-earnings optics and cash delivery during the separation year.

The pre-registered quant composite shows APTV's 12-month price momentum in the 1st percentile (worst in the S&P 500 coverage) and earnings-momentum (SUE) in the 21st percentile, corroborating that the market has not yet decided the guidance cut was a one-off.

Customer concentration (~42% of net sales from the top 5 customers, historically led by GM/Stellantis/Ford/VW) is real in a soft, uneven global auto-production environment (China down, EMEA down 7% in Q1'26); this figure is a secondary-source citation not independently re-verified against the primary 10-K footnote in this pass.
data_conflicts: Triage's cited '17% FCF yield' (from Yahoo/d4's trailing freeCashflow field) is stale and still includes the now-divested Electrical Distribution Systems (Versigent) business; on the post-spin, continuing-operations FY2026 guide (FCF $625-725m midpoint on a $9.48bn market cap) the real FCF yield is approximately 7.1%, well below the cited figure.

SEC XBRL quarterly revenue tags mix an 'as-originally-reported' (consolidated, including EDS) and a 'restated for discontinued operations' (continuing-ops only) basis depending on which filing last touched that period (e.g. Q2'25 shown at $3,199m restated vs Q3'25 at $5,212m not-yet-restated) -- resolved in the dossier by using only like-for-like, company-disclosed continuing-operations figures and flagging the mixed-basis trap explicitly.
APTV.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium -- the statistical cheapness and improved balance sheet are real, but a same-quarter guidance cut across every metric plus bottom-percentile momentum mean the thesis has not yet been confirmed by a clean quarter

FIS.thesis_one_line: Bank core-processing giant swapped a non-cash-generating Worldpay stake for a big, high-margin issuer-processing business -- cheap, but now more levered and integrating.
kill_criteria: Adjusted-EPS guidance is cut again at the Q3'26 or Q4'26 release (any reduction to the low end of the current $6.15-6.24 range).
Gross leverage fails to decline toward the 2.8x target -- stays at or above 3.5x for two consecutive quarters after Q2'26.
Client attrition (UBS/Credit-Suisse-style losses) widens beyond the currently disclosed ~1-point drag on 2026 revenue growth.
Capital Markets segment professional-services revenue declines for a third consecutive quarter (currently -17% in the most recent disclosed quarter).
Share buybacks remain fully paused beyond FY2027 -- i.e. management fails to resume 'meaningful' repurchases once leverage nears its own 2.8x target, contradicting its own stated plan.
key_adverse_facts: Gross leverage was 3.5x at June 30, 2026 (company-stated), above its own 2.8x target, and management has 'temporarily curtailed share repurchases and paused tuck-in M&A activity to accelerate deleveraging' -- a real, current capital-allocation constraint.

Adjusted-EPS guidance was cut at the Q2'26 release (to $6.15-6.24 / 7.0-8.5% growth, from $6.22-6.32 / 8-10% growth given at Q4/FY'25), alongside cuts to pro forma revenue growth (5.1-5.7% to 4.5-5.0%) and pro forma EBITDA growth (7.2-8.4% to 5.9-6.9%) -- a mixed, net-negative revision even though free-cash-flow guidance was simultaneously raised $100m.

Q1'26 GAAP diluted EPS of $4.58 is dominated by a ~$2.2bn one-time pre-tax gain on the Worldpay stake sale and is not a run-rate figure; Q2'25 GAAP EPS was a loss of -$0.90/share -- the GAAP-to-adjusted gap here is wide and must never be blended with adjusted EPS.

A $210m securities class-action settlement (In re FIS Securities Litigation, alleging misleading statements about the PRIOR Worldpay acquisition's integration/synergies, 2020-2023) received final court approval on 2026-07-09 -- resolved and largely insurance-covered, but directly relevant precedent given the current deal's own integration/synergy claims are similarly central to the thesis.

Capital Markets segment sales are running behind plan (slower backlog-to-revenue conversion, professional-services revenue -17%) and UBS/Credit-Suisse-related client attrition is cutting ~1 percentage point off 2026 revenue growth -- current-quarter operational softness, not a distant risk.
data_conflicts: Triage cited 'net debt/EBITDA of 5.8x is elevated' as the main red flag; the company's own Q2'26 earnings call states gross leverage was 3.5x at June 30, 2026 (target 2.8x). This dossier uses the primary-source 3.5x figure; the triage number appears to be either a stale pre-close estimate or a different leverage definition and was not independently reconciled to 5.8x in this pass.
FIS.confidence_in_thesis: medium -- the strategic and valuation case is well evidenced from primary filings, but elevated leverage, a fresh guidance cut and real segment-level softness (Capital Markets, client attrition) are current, unresolved risks that argue for a starter position
